annotations.topic: H126 DTEK Renewables EBITDA +100% ($104m) vs Thermal Strikes
annotations.note: DTEK Renewables H126 rev +92% YoY to $133m, EBITDA doubled to $104m (78% margin); DTEK Energy remains CCC-/CC under NBU FX transfer controls and thermal plant strikes.
Revenues secured by long-term Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) or regulated tariff frameworks, providing hard-currency indexation and guaranteed minimum volume off-take.
Heavy generation transition capex peaks in 2024-2025; multi-year FCF inflects strongly positive as commercial operations commence.
Strategic national utility champions benefit from government balancing accounts or explicit fuel supply guarantees, mitigating commodity price volatility.
DTEK O&G restructured $425m bond to Dec-2029 at 9.875%; DTEK Renewables rated CC by Fitch on €281m Nov-2027 green bond refi risk.

verdict.stance: Distressed Hold / Wartime Infrastructure Damage vs Tariff Caps & Renewables Surge
verdict.summary: DTEK Energy (Fitch CCC- / Moody's Caa3) posted FY24 revenue of UAH 57.8bn (~$520m EBITDA) and ~$660m Fitch-projected FY25 EBITDA under raised price caps, though thermal plants suffer ongoing strikes ahead of 2027 Eurobond maturities. Sister unit DTEK Renewables doubled 1H26 EBITDA to $104m but carries CC-rated €281m Nov-27 green bonds constrained by NBU FX transfer rules.

positives: DTEK Oil & Gas achieved consensual $425m bond restructuring extending to Dec-2029 at 9.875% coupon.
NBU cross-border FX transfer relaxations opened pathways for certain coupon servicing.
negatives: DTEK Renewables Fitch 'CC' rating on €281m green bond maturing November 2027 refinancing risk.
Ongoing Russian drone/missile strikes on DTEK thermal power & grid assets.
Siloed ring-fencing and NBU capital-control friction.
